To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the active behaviour and the passive behaviour of the myocardial tissue is well captured using a micromorphic material model, that the active behaviour is highly dependent on both the initial fibre orientation and the director field, that the director field can be used to describe the direction of the active stress and that a micromorphic description can be used to model the behaviour of the myocardum during a heartbeat.
We have developed a computational model that can describe the behaviour of the myocardial tissue.
The use of a director field allows us to describe the behaviour of cardiac tissue in more detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a computational model of the left ventricles based on a micromorphic description and an active stress law.
the development and application of computational models for the simulation of the passive and active behaviour of cardiac tissue.
the development of a micromechanically based model of cardiac tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the micromorphic formulation presented in this study can be used to describe the passive and active response of cardiac muscle tissue during a heartbeat.
the micromorphic model used in this study is a suitable and realistic representation of the myocardium.
the micromorphic formulation is a promising approach to model cardiac tissue and to investigate ventricular mechanics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new computational method for modelling cardiac mechanics based on a micromorphic material description.
we have successfully modelled active contraction of the left Ventricle using a micromorphic description of cardiac tissue.

micromorphic models are capable of describing the complex behaviour of the myocardial tissue.
the micromorphic formulation is able to capture the complex deformations of cardiac tissue during the cardiac cycle.
the micromorphic continuum model is able to describe cardiac tissue mechanics in a more realistic way than a classical continuum model.
